utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours and everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al., thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. Today is Wednesday. I'd like to greet Mr. Stringer, Mr. Longone, Defence counsel, and all the other members of the OTP. Registrar and the usher, we are starting late because there was a fire drill. This is why we are only starting at a half past 3.00 today. We discovered a few moments ago that the Prosecution had sent us a mail concerning their witness schedule. We have not had time to look at it. If we do have time, we'll address it today. Otherwise, it will be on Monday, but we have received your mail. For the time being we shall resume your cross-examination and have one single break at 5.00. It will be a 30-minute break, and we will then resume at half past 5.00 and run on till 7.00. And we will, I'm sure, continue tomorrow if we haven't finished by then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everyone in and around the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. Let me focus today --

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Let me focus today to the work of the coordinating committee that we have been discussing or your testimony was about on Monday and Tuesday, and in that respect could you please focus your attention on Exhibit 1D 01324 [sic]. And for the benefit of everyone in the courtroom, the Prosecution exhibits are in the -- in the big binder, and the Defence exhibits are in the first binder, and there is the first one you have there in your hands. Sir, that's the exhibit I want to refer to. 1D 01324 -- 28. And, sir, this document dated 8 October -- did you find it? Do you have it with you?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: This exhibit refers to the -- the establishing of the coordinating committee for the collection and reception of humanitarian aid, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the title says, "Collection -- or, rather, reception and distribution of humanitarian aid."

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: All right, sir. And the decision of establishing this coordinating committee was on the 8th October 1992, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And in -- in Article I of that decision, the second para, it says that, "The committee shall consist of one representative from each humanitarian organisation registered in the municipality of Mostar ..." isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And, sir, would you agree with me in the second graph it says once the president and vice-president from that committee are elected by the committee members they need to have the approval, they need to be approved by the Office for Social and Medical Welfare and Refugees from the HVO, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the article says in keeping with the approval of the social and medical welfare and refugees office since the decision is made as soon as approval is granted by the office and in keeping with the meaning and purpose of adopting such a decision at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: All right, sir. And paragraph VI of that decision it says that for items I and II basically the distribution -- the collection, reception, distribution of the humanitarian aid, those functions of the committee shall be carried out by the council of the Office for Humanitarian and Social Welfare of the HVO, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't see the word "HVO" being used here. In order to set up the committee in the sense of paragraph I and II of this decision the functions of the committee will be performed by the council of the social welfare office. So somebody had to initiate this whole action and somebody had to take the first steps and that precisely was in reference to this body.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Right, sir. And would you agree with me that that council of the office for humanitarian and social welfare belonged to the Herceg-Bosna government?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It belonged to the Mostar municipal government.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And the Mostar municipal government was governed from the Herceg-Bosna government, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And -- thank you very much. And if you see at the end of that same decision, you have the signature of Jadran Topic and clearly it says the president of the HVO municipality Mostar, isn't? HVO. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it's there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I don't know if there is a misunderstanding or a mistranslation. The Prosecution has asked you the following question, whether the government of the municipality in Mostar is the same as the government of Herceg-Bosna. You answered by saying, Yes. I don't understand any more if that's the case. Could you clarify this for us, please? It says yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] the question, Your Honour, was whether the government of Mostar municipality belonged to Herceg-Bosna, and my answer in that sense was yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Government of Herceg-Bosna, because in the question it said government of Herceg-Bosna. That's on line 2, page 4. There might have been a confusion here. The municipality is one thing, and the government of Herceg-Bosna is another. Do we agree on this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Those are two distinct authorities. There is the municipal level and there's a higher level.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And you have understood correctly my question. The Mostar -- the HVO Mostar government belonged to the Herceg-Bosna government. And, sir, now focusing your attention on --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, again the gentleman -- the gentleman yesterday and perhaps I was too calm, too nice to the gentleman and didn't react strongly enough. The gentleman needs to understand what is meant by government and what is Herceg-Bosna and what is the Herceg-Bosna government; and he keeps mixing them up. I understand maybe he wants to fit it into some kind of a theory of his, but I would ask that the Trial Chamber instruct my learned friend to be precise in his questions, and if he doesn't know, if he doesn't know the distinction between one and the other, we can give him at some point, perhaps during the break, a lesson, but this is -- this happened over and over again yesterday. I think he's trying to trick the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, if you had two more seconds of patience, you saw that I was about to do this, but you took the floor because you -- you like to and because you wanted, apparently, to be nattier than yesterday, which I'm quite sure is not necessary. I have rather the feeling that what we are faced with is a linguistic difficulty. And indeed I will tell you, Mr. Longone, the -- you have -- you have been a recidivist because there had just been a correction saying that the municipality of Mostar and the government of the municipality of Mostar is part of Herceg-Bosna, full stop, not of the government of Herceg-Bosna. And you should perhaps cross out the word "government" in your vocabulary for some time unless you have really solid ground to use it. On the merits Mr. Karnavas is quite right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I'm not going to use the word government and I understood that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Witness, if you focus to 1D 02662. That's the chart that you discussed in your testimony before on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And this is the chart that you mentioned the persons that did that chart, and it bears your signature. And in this chart you mentioned there were not -- although they were part at one point of the coordinating committee, the Merhamet and the Red Crescent are not in this chart, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's obvious, isn't it? They're not. But a mere six different organisations are listed here. I'm looking at the document. I don't know what its number is, but you see that the Red Crescent is admitted to the board as the tenth member. Therefore, this is the first chart that was drawn up, and each of the organisations that were registered throughout Mostar municipality was a member of this board, including the Red Crescent, including Merhamet, and a number of other organisations active throughout Mostar municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Yes, sir. And if ou focus on the note of that chart, would you agree with me that the centre of social work is not a member of the coordinating committee but as a specialised institution it takes part in its work.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They drew up the minutes for these meetings. They provided any technical assistance whenever necessary. Everything we've been talking about for the last two days it's about establishing criteria and all the elements that allowed this board to work as efficiently as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And if we continue with Exhibit 1D 01427 that is another exhibit that you had been discussing, sir, before.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the number?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Yes, of course. 1D 01427.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: All right. This document is a report, we can see. It's coming from the office of expelled persons, refugees, and displaced persons, the ODPR. Do you remember, sir, who was on January 1993 the head of the ODPR?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sir, this report mentions a meeting held on January 7, 1993, of all humanitarian organisations in the territory of the Herceg-Bosna community, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and there is a list of people there participating in this meeting. Do you recognise yourself in that document, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I do. Number 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And, sir, in this list we can see that there are representatives from the UNHCR, from the ICRC, from Caritas; right?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And the Merhamet, the Red Crescent, the Mostar Red Cross, and the information office.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Do you know who was the member of the information office, what information office is that one?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is someone from the office for refugees and displaced persons, the person who was in charge of spreading information in this particular office.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sir, and all these people in this meeting has to do with this coordinating committee meetings regarding the humanitarian aid?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We held meetings of the coordinating committee that weren't the same things as the meetings we had with the office for refugees. This was a general invitation to all these organisations, and it had to do with global issues. As for the functioning of the coordinating committee, we had special meetings called by the committee itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And, sir, do you recognise all the people in that -- in that list? Do you remember them?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, aside from the foreigners who came and went. I don't quite remember them all that clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And the people from -- I would say that you were mentioning that you were very much in contact and exchanging information, you told us on Monday and Tuesday, with people from the ICRC and from other international humanitarian organisations as the UNHCR. Do you remember whether these people were regularly participating in these meetings? At least in the month of January?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on this record you can see that they were there. This report is not a report from a meeting of the coordinating committee to begin with. They were invited, and they came. As for the meetings of our coordinating committee, they were under no commitment to attend those. Only if they were specially invited.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: All right. And -- but you mentioned before that -- what I understood from the transcript that these meetings called maybe by ODPR all the people, all these humanitarian organisations were invited. So it was not the only one. I understood correct that these meetings were held regularly as well?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when and how frequently the office for refugees and displaced persons of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna called such meetings. Whenever I was invited to attend on behalf of the Red Cross or the coordinating committee I would attend, but this is no meeting of the coordinating committee, and I think the two need to be kept apart.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And -- for that clarification. If you see there at the end of the list of people participating it clearly says that the next meeting has been scheduled for the 12th January 1993 at 11 hours.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: So it seems -- thank you very much. So it seems that there were other meetings that were being taking place with these people.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what this suggests, yes, but again every time I was called to a meeting I would go.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And in the conclusions of that meeting, sir, it is clear that there are some communication problems between some local humanitarian organisations and -- at the municipal level. This is what it says from the conclusions and it points out to Caritas and Merhamet, isn't it? That's in point three of the conclusion, the last point of the conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what it says, doesn't it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, do you agree with those conclusions? Do you agree there were problems with Merhamet and Caritas and communication in January 1993 regarding humanitarian aid issues?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were communication problems, but that applied to all the organisations, but these were operative problems and not some broader problems as it derived when, how, were the necessary documents secured in time for the aid to come through, that sort of problem. Were the goods distributed in a timely manner? Was there enough manpower to do the loading and unloading of aid? Operative problems, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sir, you don't remember whether there were any other concerns highlighted by the units here or the ICRC or the Merhamet in January 1993 in Mostar regarding the distribution of humanitarian aid? Is that your answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I want to object to the form of the question. He was asked a question regarding the insufficient contacts. Now when you look at the next question, it assumes facts not in evidence. I will look at the argument -- the answer that the gentleman gave, but I do think that the next question misses a beat. He's jumping to a conclusion. There are no facts to establish that. Now, if I wishes to establish some facts or show the gentleman some facts that's another story.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall any other problem regarding humanitarian or concern regarding humanitarian aid and distribution in January 1993 in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think my memory goes that far back in order to allow me to remember specific problems like that. Whatever problems we had as a humanitarian organisation we dealt with at meetings of our coordinating committee and the committee did some really good work up until the outbreak of clashes between the Croats and the Bosniaks in Mostar town itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: All right, sir. Well, let me refresh your recollection and I'm going to show you a report from the British Battalion of United Nations, dated 22nd January 1993, and it's regarding these meetings in where the organisation, yourself or someone else from your organisation at the ICRC attended with the ODPR. This is Exhibit P 01259.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Before we move to the next exhibit, Your Honour, I don't mean to disrupt too much, but we've been looking at a document that has not been admitted into evidence as an exhibit that is 1D 01427, and it is one page, as we can see. Now, a similar -- the same document, the same document with two pages has been admitted. So the second page -- this one document that is being -- that was shown doesn't have, and that is 1D 01522. I take it this was a -- 1522 is the one that has been admitted as an exhibit. I take it this must be an oversight, but -- and this is for the record. So perhaps that could be checked. But 1522 is an exhibit. 1427 is not. 1427 lacks the second page. The only reason I'm mentioning this is because I think it would be good if we are going to be showing documents to the witness it would be good to have the entire document in order for them to look at it to see whether they need to put it into context.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Can I continue my cross-examination? I appreciate your reference to those documents and we're going to check it and come back to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sir we were referring to Exhibit P 01259 and you mentioned that you didn't remember so I -- just for the benefit of refreshing your recollection, I'm -- and remember which were the concerns of international community at that time. Do you have the exhibit in front of you, sir, now?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the number? I have a lot of binders here, but I'm fumbling around with so it's difficult for me to track all these documents now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Exhibit P 01259. P 01259. And at the end of -- you first have the English version and behind it you have the B/C/S version, sir.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I've got that document now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Paragraph 1 it refers to a meeting held at the UNHCR Split on the morning of the 22nd January 1993, and from that meeting a series of problems were pointed out by the people attending there and that apparently will affect the work of the humanitarian organisations and the distribution of humanitarian aid, among others. And if you -- if you see paragraph second of the same document, sir, you see that there it says that the Mostar units CR field officer attended a meeting on Wednesday, 20 January, chaired by Mr. Tadic, minister appointed by Mate Boban, to coordinate assistance in Herceg-Bosna. Do you -- do you recall now Mr. Darinko Tadic -- Mr. Tadic, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And the paragraph continues saying the meeting included municipality representatives from as far as field as Jablanica, Prozor, Livno, Tomislavgrad, and Doboj, and the field officer was told that in future all aid deliveries were to be made directly to the local government and all aid deliveries were to be made directly -- sorry, not to the theoretically ethnically neutral coordinating committee. Sir, do you remember that there were concerns by the Merhamet and by the other participants, international organisations on that committee, of all the neutrality of that committee, of that coordinating committee at that time?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you will allow me, sir, this is the report from the second meeting, not from the one that we have just spoken about. So that I wouldn't know what meeting that was. This was on the 20th of January, probably of the same year. Yes, it was. And there were representatives of other municipalities. There were no representatives of Mostar there. So I don't know what the reason was for this statement, for this reaction, or for any kind of conclusion. And as far as the work of our coordination committee is concerned, it worked really well and I told you up until when. We had an absolute coordination and in my diary you can find all information or notes on -- as to how many, when we held meetings, who was present, and what were the topics of the conversations at our meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, just to make sure, because this meeting was attended by all international representatives or -- sorry, field offices working in the southern Bosnia region which include Mostar and my question about regarding humanitarian issues was not only related to the beginning of January 1993, but I asked you in January 1993 before. So do you remember any concern regarding the neutrality of that theoretically ethnic neutral coordinating committee in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see anywhere here that the theoretically ethnically biased coordination committee relates to Mostar. I really don't know what you're asking me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sir, let's continue with paragraph 2. After this meeting called by Mr. Darinko Tadic, it says that the implication of this is that the UNHCR would be delivering to only one faction, HVO, and relying on that faction to pass and share to the others the humanitarian aid basically. There is no much confidence that this would happen at present, and as ever no concern was shown by the HVO for the fate of the Muslims. Do you recall, sir, that there were problems about the distribution of humanitarian aid and the concerns of the Merhamet and the international organisations?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I've never seen this document before, and it's very hard for me to see any of the things that you are talking about. If you want any information about the work of the committee I can only repeat the details from my testimony yesterday and the day before yesterday, and that's all I know with regard to any other activities, but the coordination committees existed in Livno and some other municipalities, and Mostar was not the only municipality that had such a body.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: All right, sir. I'm going to continue refreshing your recollection. The consumption of aid, this is not a new problem says the report. The consumption of aid put into municipality warehouse by a coordinating committee -- sir --

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Could you please direct me to the part from which you're reading? I'd like to be able to follow if that's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Of course it's not a problem. It's paragraph second. We are still on para second of that same exhibit, sir. And the last part of paragraph second says the concerns about the neutral -- theoretical ethnically neutral coordinating committees. It says, "This is not a new problem the consumption of aid put into municipality warehouse by a coordinating committee has always been difficult to ascertain. "A significant quantity general favours one side, reaches one or more army and the black market, as well as supports refugees. This limitation on delivery could be expected to apply throughout the area designated as provinces 8 and 10 in the proposed Geneva agreement. The office was also informed that if UNHCR declined to comply with this instruction," delivering the aid to the HVO government to Mr. Tadic, "The HVO would close the border at Matkovic to UNHCR traffic." And, sir, if you go to paragraph 3. Sir, if you go to paragraph 3 of the same exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. What is -- why do you want to intervene, Mr. Praljak? THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] It is my wish to read everything. We keep on dwelling upon the first page and it's very hard for any of us to know what this is all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And perhaps while we're looking at that first page, Your Honour, paragraph 2, perhaps my learned friend could point to the gentleman the part about Doboj and whether representatives from Doboj would have been there, recognising where Doboj was and still remains but who was occupying Doboj at the time, whether representatives for Doboj from Doboj would have been in Mostar at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Shall I continue with my cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue. However, Mr. Registrar, can you make sure that you move the B/C/S text to the right place so that the accused can see the entire document in their language especially paragraphs 5, 6 and 7 so they have an overall view of the entire document. Yes, proceed, Mr. Longone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: So in paragraph 3 of the same exhibit the last sentence of paragraph 3 starting with HVO. Do you see that, sir? [B/C/S spoken]. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I really did not participate in such meetings. Everything I might say from now on would be just taking things out of the context and telling you stories that I really don't know. Any assistance that I received from anybody I made sure that it was ready for distribution, and this is something that happened before any aid entered the territory and I wouldn't be able to tell you anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sir, you were the Red Cross representative for Mostar from 1992 June till 1998. You continued working in the Red Cross until 2003. I'm not asking whether you participated in this meeting now. My question was whether you were aware of the concerns of the distribution of humanitarian aid and in this respect, sir, I'm going to read you that last sentence that you already have identified: "HVO members in Mostar have threatened to blow up the UNHCR office if they continue to supply Muslims."

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never heard this before, and I've never seen it before, of course. UNHCR was a permanent partner of the Red Cross and all the other of humanitarian organisations that were active in the coordination committee, and we -- the -- the reaction at this meeting never reflected on our further work never before the month of April, the month of May when this reaction was connected with the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sir, in this report they are referring to threats to the UNHCR personnel and to the delivery of, you know, affecting basically the delivery of humanitarian aid. Do you remember any incident either in January or in February where the UNHCR has been attacked or that you can tell that those threats were actually took place in Mostar or around Mostar? You were dealing with humanitarian aid at that time. Do you remember anything?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Let's go to Exhibit P 01462. This -- 01462. All right. Well, let's continue. Sir, my apologies. Let's continue with the following exhibit. Do you find it there, do you know?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] This is only two. [Interpretation] I have not been able to locate the relevant document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: We will come back to it. Thank you very much, sir. Let's focus on the -- on the decrees -- on the decisions taken on the 15 and 29 April, 1993, sir. Those were exhibits P 01894. P 01894. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Yes. [Interpretation] I have the document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: You have -- this is the decision from the municipality of Mostar regarding the changing on the status of refugees and expellees. We have -- you have discussed this decision before in the courtroom. Do you remember now?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About this decision, yes, I'm aware of it. I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And, sir, in that decision is this true that you had to distribute the humanitarian aid, the Herceg-Bosna, Red Cross from Mostar had to distribute the humanitarian aid according to this decision and to this criteria?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And, sir, they said in that decision, in point III, that previously issued cards cease to be valid and new family card will be issued in the Mostar Centre For Social Work, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how I read it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And, sir, basically people that were located in abandoned flats at that time, the refugees and expellees that were occupying abandoned flats in Mostar, they had to leave those flats and move to collective centres, isn't it, by this decision?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this decision, only the internally displaced persons, i.e., those who were able to return to their liberated homes, to put it that way. It applied to them. They were supposed to return to their original places of residence. It did not apply to the refugees and expellees proper.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And, sir, and they have 15 days, or it was -- it would take 15 days to apply this decision -- to comply with this decision, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if it's in the text, then I suppose that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sorry, sir. It's para IV of that decision. If you see it at the end of para IV of the that decision it says items listed in that decision shall be done within 15 days of the adoption of this decision.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see it. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Para IV?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it but I don't know what you question is, and I don't know how to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: My question was would you agree with me, sir, that in para IV it says that this decision will be implemented or done within 15 days of the date of adoption of it? Isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every decision that was valid had its implementation deadline and an institution that was in charge of its implementation. That's why all this information is contained within the body of this text as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Prlic. THE ACCUSED PRLIC: [Interpretation] I really don't want to intervene, but this is going beyond any point. For the second time the witness is asked something that is not reflected in the text. I'm reading the text like everybody else in the courtroom, and in Article IV you can see that it refers to schools very clearly, that people have to move out of the schools within 15 days. In his question the Prosecutor distorts that, just like a while ago and on page 15, line 19, he himself reading that text of the Exhibit P 01259, he read the HVO government although the word government does not exist in the text. I would kindly ask the Prosecutor to adhere to the text when putting his questions, because the record does not reflect the veracity of the exhibits that we have before us at the same time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor, Mr. Prlic points out that paragraph IV of the decision refers to schools and that there was a deadline of 14 days, but that would apply to schools. Does this change anything to your approach?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Maybe -- maybe if you read -- if we read para IV, it clearly refers to paragraph I, II, and III. So basically people that are living in abandoned flats or any other places between the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Longone. I wonder whether you are not in an unnecessary error, as it were. You quote paragraph IV or numeral IV as Mr. Karnavas calls them, Roman IV. Wouldn't V be more germane to this issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And para V of that decision, sir, it says that: "This decision shall enter into effect on the date of its adoption and shall be implemented as of 15 April 1993." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Perhaps one -- if you allow. May I just -- I'm sorry. Perhaps it's the same. 15th of April. That is the same day the decision is signed. Is that -- is that correct? Would you agree? I mean, you don't have to agree because that's what we read here, unless you know doing else. Have you known about this decision?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I was aware of this decision and the implementation of this decision was not as fast as it was originally conceived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: That is very plausible indeed. Can you say more about the implementation? I'm sorry if I'm stepping on your feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor, I have a problem with the relevance of this exhibit. Indeed you mentioned the date of the entry into force of the decision, but in paragraph or Article IV, we are talking about buildings reserved for school purposes. I don't understand. So where is your point with regard to the date of entry into force of the decision regarding the expulsion of individuals, or does it have to do with the use of the premises?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. My point is that this is a decision passed on the 15 April 1993, and basically it's saying that cards for these refugees and expellees, they're going to -- they list who they're going to receive or they're only going to be issued to persons who are not staying in abandoned flats or apartments in Mostar. So basically they have to leave those flats those expellees and refugees in order to get the refugee card, which is going to be issued in the Mostar Centre for Social Work, and the ones that cannot go somewhere else, they have to be there, they are going to be accommodated in those schools which the witness yesterday in cross-examination or during -- I think in cross-examination with one of counsel said that he didn't remember whether in January -- whether in May 1993 the people were going to school or not. And at the end, as Judge Trechsel pointed out, clearly they have a very limited time to comply with this decision. These are people in need, and we were referring to the fact -- the witness referred that there were 30.000 or 38.000 people in Mostar, that there were more than 8.000 refugees, children and women, and they were given such a short period of time to get out of these apartments. That's the relevance of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Let me try to be of some assistant here to all the parties and to the establishment of the truth. We must distinguish two things, obviously, and I come back to you, Witness. We have this issue of the schools, and there there's a deadline of 14 -- 15 days until which the school must be vacated. In paragraph V, the entry into force is fixed as -- or, rather, the implementation as of 15 April. It does not mean -- it does not say by 15 April but as of, and maybe the interpreters can assist in explaining whether there is this difference in the original text. But I have asked a question of the witness which then was passed under the carpet, and I'll draw it from the carpet. I'll ask you, Mr. Simunovic, can you give us an indication as to whether and, if so, in what time space this decision was actually implemented as far as apartments are concerned and as far as schools are concerned, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you allow me, Your Honour, I would like to give you my perspective of this decision, what its intention was, especially from the point of view of my position and need to distribute the humanitarian aid to those in need. This was the time when there wasn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Simunovic, but we have to keep in order, and I would like you to answer my question, which does not go to the explanation of why these were, but how did the implementation run? Was it implemented, and by which time, at what catence for both eventualities, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have the exact indicators. I can't tell you because it was a long time ago, but I know that displaced persons from the territory of the municipality referred to under item II, those were internally displaced persons. They were not refugees and expellees. Anybody who was able to return to their abandoned homes did so, or they filed a request to help them with construction and building materials or in any other way or form to help them prepare their house for return. The implementation of this decision for the category of users under II was launched on this date, and the implementation lasted for a while after that. And it says under III that the IDs were withdrawn and that people would be renew -- reissued new IDs, which is only normal, if they return to their original place of residence. As far as item IV is concerned, it applied exclusively -- exclusively to the refugees, expellees who were accommodated in collective accommodation, i.e., in schools and other educational facilities. The reason was the beginning of that school year an urgent reaction was called for. However, the Prosecutor, in his questions, said that people who left these facilities wouldn't nowhere to be accommodated. And it says clearly here that they would be accommodated at other collective accommodation facilities, and that's how this decision was implemented. This decision refers to three categories of people, military -- militarily able-bodied men, internally displaced persons, and refugees and expellees who were accommodated in collective accommodation. The decision came into force on this day, and its implementation was taking place for a while on the ground. And let's just understand that 20 or so days after the issuing of this decision the conflict broke out. So it is really questionable to which extent this decision could be implemented.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'd like to put a question to you but from another perspective, seen from the respective authorities of the HVO and of the municipality. Let's look at this decision. We shall notice that Mr. Topic makes decisions that have to do with the fate of displaced people, expellees, and refugees. Paragraph number II, he says therein that people from Mostar -- or that in Mostar and that hail from other liberated municipalities have to return to their own municipalities. So Mr. Topic was of the view that he had the power to regulate the movements of people. Such a decision, was that not within the purview of the HVO government, which had another authority than that of a municipal body that sees problems only from the perspective of the municipality? Here, however, we can see that Mr. Topic takes it on himself to say that a refugee hailing, say, from Jablanica, a Croat, would have to return to Jablanica if Jablanica was liberated. That's just an example. So looking at this document, I wonder what is the scope of the powers of the HVO government and of the municipality. You were in Mostar, and you had a position within the Red Cross. And who had the last word, the final word on the issue of displaced persons, expellees, and refugees? Was it the municipality or was it the HVO government?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I understand what you're saying. If we look at paragraph II of this decision, the entire text here is in reference to persons from Mostar municipality. Mr. Topic wasn't doing anything that was outside the framework of Mostar municipality. We look at paragraph IV. Likewise, these were people who were put up within Mostar municipality in schools. What this decision does, it makes sure they have sufficient accommodation, again in Mostar municipality, but this time round at a different location. Therefore, this decision is only to be understood as the responsibility of the person who had it adopted, and I don't believe that in the case at hand the person that went beyond their powers or authority. And all of this is in reference to Mostar municipality alone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And, Witness, just to recap on this and to continue, you said you have to apply this decision. The Red Cross from Herceg-Bosna Mostar had to apply this decision when distributing humanitarian aid. That's what you said before, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. As yesterday, I would really like to ask you one thing. When you're talking about the Mostar municipality Red Cross --

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Excuse me sir.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please just make --

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir I am the one putting questions to you. You are the witness and I'm the Prosecution and my question was just to recap on the issue that was discussed, you said you have to apply this decision from Mostar municipality in the distribution of humanitarian aid and you said yes, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And, sir --

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise. Perhaps you've got me wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sir, and in paragraph I, in order to get the card that will allow you to get the humanitarian aid, you have to move out from abandoned apartments, were not staying in abandoned apartments, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So cards for refugees and displaced persons were only awarded to persons between 1 and 17 years of age. Men over 60 years of age and women over 55 years of age who were not staying in an abandoned flat and had arrived from one of the occupied areas of Bosnia-Herzegovina or the Republic of Croatia. This card shall not be awarded to persons arriving from elsewhere in Mostar municipality, from non-occupied areas of the Republic of Croatia or Bosnia and Herzegovina. It is stated here with the greatest of clarity what age group this refers to and what type of accommodation these persons would be entitled to. This decision partly has to do with paragraph II as well. Internally displaced persons living in abandoned flats were meant to go back to their own original areas. The rest of them were supposed to monitor the age group stated here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. And if we can move now to Exhibit 1D 01083. 1D -- that's in the small -- in that -- in that binder. Yes, sir. 1D 01083. This exhibit was discussed early in this week with you, and it refers to -- to the issuing of refugee cards, but in this case it's not Mostar but is in Jablanica, and it's dated 19 March 1993. Sir, would you agree with me that in paragraph I of this order it says that: "Until further notice, the Red Cross shall issue refugee cards with temporary residence to refugees and displaced persons who are not military conscripts and arrive in Jablanica municipality after ... the order of 10 March 1993 ..." It's referring that in this case, the Red Cross shall issue refugee cards, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what was going on in Jablanica. That's what the document claims, and I have no reason to disbelieve what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: So basically in Mostar it was the social welfare office that will distribute or will issue the refugee cards, and here in Jablanica was the Red Cross. That's what the difference are.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was done by one and the same person. The gentleman who was in charge of the Red Cross was a social worker in Jablanica municipality at the same time. Two positions, and one person alone, Nedzad Mucic [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, if we now go to the big binder, the one that bears the Prosecution exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before moving on to the next binder, Witness, there's something I don't understand. Yesterday you said that the Red Cross was neutral, unbiased, impartial and so on. A certain criteria were to be abided by the Red Cross. And we now have a document which states purportedly that the municipality has given the Red Cross some orders and has stated that some cards should not be given. If the Red Cross is impartial and independent, it's for the Red Cross to hand out those cards according to its own criteria, not according to the criteria of the municipality. How can you explain this, that a municipality can give instructions to the Red Cross on the way in which it needs to manage the situation, i.e., people who are in difficulty for a number of reasons.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if we compare the two situations, Jablanica and Mostar, the number of persons in need differed dramatically between the two. The Mostar Red Cross had neither the facilities necessary nor the professional staff that would have been required to categorise all those who were in need of humanitarian aid. We received our information from technically well-versed institutions, professionals in the field, and we tried to get as much aid for distribution to all the categories mentioned by those institutions. Everything that had to do with aid for refugees, any aid that arrived from the UNHCR. It was the UNHCR that asked to speak to government bodies, and we were merely a partner in charge of reception and distribution. We were also supposed to monitor the distribution process itself on the ground, made sure that everything was delivered to whichever local communes were involved, make sure the quantities were right and check all the files. We saw yesterday how that was done. If I may, I would just like to say something else. Being involved in the collection of humanitarian aid, it almost became a profession. These people didn't have any other jobs. But they went to all the places where they thought they could get something, get humanitarian aid, in order to get it and deliver it to those in need. There had to be some sort of order. The Red Cross was not responsible for keeping order. Government institutions would have been. The authorities would have been. The Red Cross never turned away anyone who came seeking assistance whenever assistance was possible. So if you ask me, these are two different matters. I was not a government official. I was working for the Red Cross. I was doing my job. People from the Mostar HVO were also doing their jobs. And I think they were doing their jobs well. If you look at the cards, if you look at the files, if you look at the way the records were kept, they did a very good job, and much of their job was about helping us, helping us get on with our work and helping us to turn away those who were only shamming they were in need. Everybody wanted something. It was difficult to tell if someone was just shamming or someone was really a needy person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, my question did not relate to the quality of your work. I'm sure you had to face these different situations. But the question I have is how could you receive orders from the municipality in this area? That's what my question is about, because this document shows that the Red Cross needs to obey the orders. You are neutral, impartial, independent. This is what I find hard to understand. You've just told me that there were reasons for this. I am prepared to acknowledge your reasons, but from the outside it's difficult to understand that a body like yours can receive orders from a municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. President, perhaps the gentleman may be looking at the wrong document. I suspect that your question goes to the Jablanica municipality document, which is 1D 01083.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And perhaps in that context --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. My question was based on document ID 1083. Maybe you didn't have that right document in front of you. In this document the municipality gives instructions to the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Incidentally, I happen to know this, and I did say that a while ago. The person who was in charge of the Red Cross was the only official and the person responsible for social welfare in Jablanica municipality. I assume that that was the reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I understand better now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sir, you mentioned yesterday that on the 9th of May when all the people -- the Bosnian Muslim population from Mostar was -- was arrested in the Heliodrom, you mentioned that you saw that on the TV, on the evening news; if I may recall, correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Are you sure that you want -- are you sure that you wanted to say that all the Muslims people were arrested? I find that a bit going beyond what we've heard so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Bosnian Muslim people were transferred to the -- to the Heliodrom. And I remember you mentioned that you have seen that on the news or on the TV.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I explained, I got more information from the evening news than I had known the same morning when I came to work, and that's why I talked about TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: All right, sir. And going back, we were discussing the concerns about the distribution of humanitarian aid, highlighted or -- by the international organisations, and the threats posed to UNHCR workers, humanitarian aid workers, and references to Mr. Darinko Tadic. And, sir, do you remember what happened after this decision that we were discussing from changing the refugee status of -- changing the refugee status in Mostar, whether it was any public appeal on the TV or in the radio regarding this -- this decision and the effect of this decision? Do you recall anything, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: So let me refresh are your recollection. Let's go to Exhibit P 01941. Do you have the exhibit, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: All right, sir. And this -- this document is dated 18 April 1993, so three days after the decision changing the status of refugees in Mostar. It's dated Siroki Brijeg, 18 April 1993. It's addressed to all Herceg-Bosna, Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, radio and television stations. And if you see at the end of that document, at the bottom of the B/C/S version of it, it says, "Mr. Darinko Tadic, Department Head." And basically, sir, let me read the first part of this document to assist to refresh your recollection: "At a time when the Croatian people are under attack by those to whom the Croatian people have extend the hand of salvation, have cared for, protected, fed and housed in the Republic of Croatia and the area of the Herceg-Bosna community, hundreds of thousands of Muslim mothers, children, the elderly and frail, now in return for all this, their fathers and brothers are destroying and burning Croatian homes, and their families killing our women, elderly and frail. "For this reason it is realistic to expect a large number of Croats from Central Bosnia and Northern Herzegovina seeking safety, fleeing before terror. We want to use this opportunity to appeal and call on all people who have compassion for the suffering and miseries of the Croats from the areas at risk to make themselves known if they are able to offer shelter and simply help our people." And the document goes on saying that they can apply for helping them with the office of expelled -- ODPR, basically, the HVO office in Siroki Brijeg and in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point, I would object to any questions following from this particular document if he's trying to link it up earlier. Firstly he said let me refresh your recollection, and I suggest that you cannot refresh a recollection unless one has a recollection. He's indicated he didn't remember and, of course, he never stated anything and this document has nothing to do with the gentleman. Secondly, it has nothing to do with April 15th. This April 15th implementation of that particular decision, what does it have to do with this particular document? Absolutely nothing. So how is he able to link one to the other and then dare say, "Let me refresh your recollection." Now, perhaps he wishes to ask another line of questions, which may be perfectly fine, but I don't think that you can rely -- you can link one with the other. And of course we don't know where this went to. And it doesn't show that it went to the gentleman. If, for instance, this document had gone to the Mostar municipal Red Cross, you may be able to say, "Well, did you look at it, and if so, does this refresh your recollection?" But not only does it not have anything as far as the distribution list, but also if you look at the original, Your Honours, you will see that there's no signature to this. There's no stamp. There's nothing. Who created this document? How it came about, who knows? But I don't think that this is proper cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Longone, what did you do -- what did you want to do exactly? Did you want to refresh his memory, address another topic? Personally, I'm not quite sure what you wanted to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sir, we are going to get into that part of the -- of the cross-examination, but basically what I was asking the witness from the very beginning is about the concerns that international community have about the situation of humanitarian aid and about the situation in Mostar; and he didn't remember anything about the concerns that were highlighted by the UNHCR, although he has been working for UNHCR and in contact with them as he has recognised it all the time. We are talking about now of people being move out from flats in Mostar and -- there are a lot of refugees, Bosnian Muslim refugees in Mostar who have to reapply again and move out of the flats in order to get some cards, in order to get some humanitarian aid, and we have this public appeal referring to the fact that some people -- that many refugees from -- from Central Bosnia and from the north of Herzegovina are being called to come, to take refuge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again, this is a mischaracterisation of the document. And if I may use one word: Serendipity. It could be that there's just a timing of situations happening one place and another situation happening in another and to try to link it as if one has something to do with the other, I think is a far stretch.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sir -- Your Honours, if I can continue with the cross-examination and Your Honours will see where I'm trying to go with this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, just one moment. There's something which I disagree about, because you said that this is an appeal launched to the Croats so that they come and settle in Mostar or somewhere else. On reading this document, I don't read that into the document at all. Maybe you wish to link this document with ethnic cleansing with hindsight, or the other way around. Is that what you wanted to check out with this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sir -- Your Honour, we referred to this -- my apologies. We referred to this meeting in January -- at the end of January 1993 regarding the concerns of the UNHCR and the threats, and basically this document clearly is addressing the people -- the Bosnian Croat people from Central Bosnia and northern of Herzegovina, and is referring to the people that the Bosnian Croats have -- the Muslim people that they have taken care of and saying that now their fathers and brothers, they are killing them. And I just want to -- to address what was the situation in the ground at that time. I mean, all -- all these -- Witness. All these definitely would have an impact in the work of the people distributing humanitarian aid, in the threatens to the people distributing humanitarian aid and in the refugees that are in and around the territory controlled by the Herceg-Bosna authorities, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is collective thinking. I mean, and I object to this line of questioning. Let's assume -- let's assume for the sake of argument that this document is authentic, and let's assume that this individual wrote this document, and I find nothing so horrendous about it; but to suggest now that the Croats who are distributing aid would now not distribute aid to non-Croats as a result of this appeal or events that are happening some place, and to lump them all into one I think is rather outrageous and egregious, and I don't think that the gentleman has provided any foundation for this. It's not relevant and unless he can show some relevance or foundation, and we should just move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sir, could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Put your question and then we'll see. I'm listening to both parties as a Judge. I'm totally lost. Put your question and then we'll see.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Witness, is there any link between Bosnians -- moving Bosnians out and Bosnian Croats in, in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that anything like that was going on, but if I may by Your Honours' leave, the Prosecutor is asking me to have my memory jogged, and then we talked about what went on at Heliodrom, and then this document takes us back a month, and then they were asking me whether I saw something on TV or whether I saw something on radio. Believe me, I'm confused myself. I've never seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are saying that you've never seen the document. Whatever the case may be, it's time to have a break now. It is 5.00. We shall have a 30-minute break, but my colleague would like to put a question before the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I think are -- Mr. Simunovic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Well, I pressed the button. I have a blinking green light.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Judge, please. We cannot hear him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Now it's okay. And I didn't do anything to make it okay. That came from the ... Witness, I think that you have not seen this document. It's not surprising, because it has been addressed to radio and TV stations, and as far as we've heard so far, you, yourself, were neither. The question is whether you have heard about it, be it directly by listening to the radio, watching TV, be it indirectly by hearsay, by other people telling you, "Did you hear?" "I heard on the radio." Have you, in this indirect, perhaps, way have any knowledge of this appeal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Hvala ljepo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall have our one and only break for this afternoon now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sir, going back to Exhibit P 02151.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 02151, yes. Is that the exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And this is an exhibit that you have been put before, sir, and it's referring to the reasons why the Merhamet were pulling out from Mostar, coordinating committee. And it refers to -- to the decree that we have discussed before, the Mostar -- the Mostar decision regarding the changing on the refugee status. And, sir, I will address you to the exposition of the reasons and number 3 of it, and the second para -- third para after -- under that -- that point it states that: "The realisation of the third predominantly important goal, the relocation of the displaced and expelled homeless people in this way," in the way of that decree, "is not only unlawful but also contrary to the general principles of humanitarianism and public conscience." Do you remember, sir, in your meetings with the Merhamet any reference to these concern from them about the Mostar decree -- Mostar decision of April 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The problems regarding the implementation of the decision were considered at the coordination committee meetings and certain activities pertaining to our conclusions were incorporated into our subsequent decision. This conclusion in its written form was never the subject of discussions at any meetings, and Mr. Sahovic as representative at that meeting said that if the decision were to be implemented to the letter, and he was referring to the first decision, that they would consider further possibilities for Merhamet remaining on the coordination committee. I saw this document for the first time as I was proofed for this testimony and again today, now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Now, sir, when you're referring to the meeting that you have with the Merhamet, that's the same date, the 30 April 1993? To that meeting you refer to?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I meant that meeting, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sir, we have seen a couple of documents referring to the Merhamet and to the people working for the Merhamet. Have you ever heard that they were harassed or they have problems when complying with their mandate?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no. I never received any information with this regard, but I would like to say that the mandate of Merhamet differed very much from the mandate of the Red Cross. I don't want to put the two organisations at the same level and given the same status. And it is very important when distinguishing between the reactions on the part of the two organisations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sir, my question was if you recall any harassment to the people of the Merhamet. I don't want to compare with the Red Cross in Mostar. Do you recall anything about it, any concern flagged by them in the meetings you had with them?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: So I want to show you Exhibit P 03461. And do you have the exhibit, sir? P 03461.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And this is a document from the military police, 6th Company of the 1st Battalion, dated 15 July 1993. And it refers that on 15 July 1993, the vehicle and the telefax machine from Merhamet, in Ljubuski all goods has been ceased and handed over to the Criminal Investigative Service. Do you remember anything of that, sir, the seizing of goods of the Merhamet at that time?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I cooperated with the Merhamet of Mostar and I have no knowledge of any such thing. I've never heard this before or seen -- seen it. If the Prosecutor will allow me to say something that I would like to say about the Red Cross organisation. I've been inspired by this particular document. If you allow me. The premises of the Red Cross in Mostar were broken into three times between 1993 and 1996, and every time the complete documentation was destroyed as well as the computers. Their cars were stolen and so on and so forth. In other words, humanitarian organisations were often targeted because people believed that they had money, food, and other such things. What I'm saying is that I'm not establishing any links with what is contained herein, but I am just saying that we also had problems with people who looked at the whole situation in a somewhat different way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that we have the same situation again. The question implied something that really doesn't have anything to do with the document. My learned friend asked literally whether the witness remembered some situations of harassment, that people were harassed, that people -- the officials of Merhamet were harassed. This document cannot have nothing to do with harassment, because anything can be behind this document. The first could be a criminal procedure or any other such thing. There's no harassment here because this is done by legal organs who write their legal reports. It's very difficult to assume that this could be harassment. Second of all, they did not intervene against people from Merhamet. They took their vehicle and their telefax, and it transpires from this note that this was the kind of intervention that the Crime Prevention Service is often engaged in as part of their criminal investigation. So there's no way we would talk about harassment. By putting the question in that way it was suggested to the witness that this was a case of harassment or ill-treatment of the Merhamet officials. That's how I understood the question, and this does not arise from this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Prosecutor, if you speak of harassment, I suppose you have a series of facts in mind to support this. They have to be ascertained and approved by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: If I may add a question. I must confess I find this document very cryptic, because it says, "assisting criminal investigation." What kind of investigation? Against whom? Against -- against Merhamet, or did Merhamet complain that it was stolen, and then it was found somewhere and seized with a view to handing it back? I find this completely inconclusive, and unless you can put it in a context so we can understand what it really means, I'm afraid it's -- it's pretty useless. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sir, we were referring to the activity of the Merhamet, and if you see -- we have seen Exhibit 1D 2572. It's from the first binder, the small binder from the Defence. Yes. That one. 1D 2572. And you have -- you remember that you -- you mentioned -- you saw this document before, and you mentioned that you knew Mr. Zijad Demirovic.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just partially. I did not see the document, but I knew the gentleman who signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Do you know what happened with Mr. Zijad Demirovic was assisting the Merhamet here in the -- in the entering and the distribution of some humanitarian aid to the Muslims of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to this line of questioning. First of all, one has nothing to do with the other. He's trying to tie in somehow that Mr. Demirovic, because he was assisting in Merhamet, something happened to him. The gentleman happened to be the head of the regional office of the SDA, which is the Muslim political party. I do object to this. You cannot link one with the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Your Honours. Your Honours, yesterday the witness said that he found quite improper that the -- a member of the SDA was also a member of the Merhamet and assisting or working on -- with humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I like to see the page number and the line for that. He never indicated that Mr. Demirovic was working for Merhamet. He indicated quite clearly that he was the head of the regional SDA. That was -- and then there was a question from Judge Trechsel. This occurred on Monday. So I would like to have the page where there is that claim. And while we're at it, it should be noted that this is the Office Of Displaced Persons and Refugees and the seeds are coming from Croatia, from Ploce and going through.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sir -- sir, on page 33468, line 8 until line 11 of your testimony, you said: "To tell you the truth, I have never seen this document before, and I found it -- I find it very illogical to see direct involvement, direct involvement of a political party in the work of a humanitarian organisation. That never happened with our organisation." That's what you said, sir. My question, sir, is do you know what happened with Mr. Demirovic in 1993, after May 4, 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Now, sir, let's go to Exhibit 1D 02721. This is a document from Stolac, dated 13 July 1992, and they are referring to the appointment of a board for the collection of humanitarian aid. All this board for collecting humanitarian aid. And you see among the people in the board is the Merhamet. You have the Red Cross from Stolac, the Merhamet, and Caritas, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I see in the document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And, sir, do you know Mehmed Kapic?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know a single person from this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sir, so I would like to point you now to Exhibit P 04838. This document is from the Military Police Administration, dated 6 September 1993. Do you have the document with you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... do you see there, sir, that Dr. Mehmed Kapic is being transferred from the district prison in Gabela to the central military prison in Ljubuski? Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And, sir, in -- I will address you to Exhibit P 76 -- P 07605. 7605. This document is -- did you find it? It is possible that it is a bit further. There are a lot of documents on the other side as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Prosecutor, it's not in the binder.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I haven't got that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: It's not in the binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Can you please look at e-court, sir? You have the document in e-court. My apologies if it's not in the binder. I will verify what is not in the binder in the break. Sir, if you see in the document, it's dated 25 January 1994, and this is a letter referring to -- to a letter from -- addressed to Mate Boban and from the Croatian authorities referring to a letter received from a representative from the European parliament, Dr. Arie Oostalander, who is a politically very highly-placed person and who is a friend of Croatia. And in this letter he's saying that he's requesting the authorities of Croatia to intervene for a group of Muslim intellectuals imprisoned in Ljubuski. This is in 25th January 1994. And according to what he says in the letter, he says that he's convinced that those people, that the European representative, are innocent and that the Croat authorities have been holding them unlawfully? And in the list of people there, sir, you have Mr. Mehmed Kapic, and you have Zijad Demirovic. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... those are the people working for Merhamet, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is just one of the people. Mr. Kapic also worked for Merhamet. Mr. Demirovic was in the party, as far as I can tell based on the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have another objection. Again the document has been misinterpreted by the Prosecution. My learned friend says that in the letter it says that the persons in the list, if they are innocent, that they should be released, and this is a misquote. In the letter, in the second paragraph before the names, it says and I quote -- and I can't see it in the English version, I must admit. Maybe it is. It says in the Croatian version: "I would like to ask you to use your authority to remove any doubt that this was arbitrary and unlawful act and to release these people if they are innocent." Therefore, the intervention that arrived in Croatia contained information about some sort of proceedings. In this case this was a criminal proceedings which we saw in the previous documents. It doesn't say anywhere that these people are innocent and they should be released. There is a reservation expressed here, a doubt in the words, "if they are innocent, they should be released." MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't like to jump the gun or act in haste, but I believe that the Prosecution is trying to draw a conclusion that this was a person which was imprisoned unlawfully. The previous document that the Prosecution showed us calls for the transfer from the district prison in order to undertake some investigation proceedings. In the there is P 07533 which contains a worth by Mr. Biskic which refers to Mr. Kapic, who is referred to in here in which it says that an investigation has been launched against the gentleman before the competent court and before the investigation is over he cannot say whether the person is innocent or not, and in the spirit of what His Honour Trechsel said, just a little while ago, I'd like to say that we lack a whole plethora of data that would allow us to construct a conclusion.
